title: Isomorphic apex transport for the pinned degree-zero comparison
statement: Given two commutative squares with identical bottom and right maps f:X→S and g:T→S, apexes Z,P and maps j,r,p,q, and an isomorphism e:Z≅P satisfying e.hom followed by p=j and e.hom followed by q=r, there exists a natural target isomorphism v between Rr*((j tensor pullback M)[0]) and Rq*((p tensor pullback M)[0]). The first pinned single-degree base-change composite followed by v equals the second for every M. No open restriction or cartesianness is assumed. Definitions and ingredients: [def-pc-derived-base-change-map], [lem-pc-pinned-single-base-change-shift], [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition].

source.place: Tags 08HY (mate construction), 08FE (open direct image), 08DW (pullback restriction); inherited argument of lem-pc-open-pinned-single-degree-zero-square.

proof.text: Substitute the two projection equalities. Form the direct-image composition isomorphism k as the right-adjoint mate of the pinned pullback comparison c(e,q). Apply the single tensor counit factorization under e to obtain t. Whisker k by the single tensor source, reassociate, and whisker t by Rq to construct v. Naturality of k moves the final tensor counit through k. Insert c(e,p) inverse followed by c(e,p); functoriality cancels them. Derived base-change pasting rewrites the first factors as the base-change map for p,q followed by Rq of the unit of e. The single tensor counit factorization then rewrites the remaining factors to Rq of the tensor counit for p. This is exactly the required pinned single composite equality.

lean.statement:
theorem open_pinned_single_degree_zero_apex
    [∀ Y : Scheme.{u},
      HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Y.toRingedSpace))]
    [∀ {Y Z : Scheme.{u}} (k : Y ⟶ Z), (Scheme.Modules.tensorPullback k).Additive]
    {X S Z P T : Scheme.{u}} (f : X ⟶ S) (g : T ⟶ S)
    (j : Z ⟶ X) (r : Z ⟶ T) (p : P ⟶ X) (q : P ⟶ T)
    (h : j ≫ f = r ≫ g) (hP : p ≫ f = q ≫ g)
    (e : Z ≅ P) (hj : e.hom ≫ p = j) (hr : e.hom ≫ q = r) :
    ∃ v : singleDegreeBaseChangeTarget.{u, w} j r 0 ≅
        singleDegreeBaseChangeTarget.{u, w} p q 0,
      ∀ M : X.Modules,
        singleDegreeBaseChangeComposite f g j r h 0 M ≫ v.hom.app M =
          singleDegreeBaseChangeComposite f g p q hP 0 M
